# AQI standards in AirAtlas

Every standard is computed from stored raw concentrations at read or ingestion time. Breakpoints live in JSON tables (`aqi-engine/src/airatlas_aqi/tables/`), and these pages are generated from those tables.

| Standard | Used for | Scale | Pollutants | Averaging | Sub-index |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [CPCB NAQI](in_cpcb_naqi.md) | tamil_nadu (default), kerala (default) | 0–500 | PM10, PM2.5, NO₂, SO₂, NH₃, Pb, CO, O₃ | 8h_max24, 24h | linear (continuous) |
| [UBA LQI](de_uba_lqi.md) | germany (default) | 5 levels | NO₂, PM10, PM2.5, O₃, SO₂ | 1h | banded |
| [European AQI](eu_eaqi.md) | germany, all regions (common scale) | 6 levels | PM2.5, PM10, O₃, NO₂, SO₂ | 1h | banded |
| [UAE EAQI](ae_eaqi.md) | uae (default) | 0–500 | O₃, CO, SO₂, NO₂, PM10, PM2.5 | 1h, 8h, 24h | linear (US-EPA segments) |
| [WHO PM2.5](who_2021_pm25.md) | all regions (common scale) | 6 levels | PM2.5 | 24h | banded |

Why the same air gets different labels: India's CPCB 'Satisfactory' band reaches 60 µg/m³ PM2.5 (24 h), while WHO's 2021 guideline is 15 and the European index calls anything above 15 µg/m³ (hourly) 'Moderate' or worse. Cross-country comparisons therefore always use a common scale.
